about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: New since the model: trade-deal headlines point to firmer US export demand, while Texas growers report low yields and high fuel costs that reinforce the abandonment story. Old-crop Dec is near 79 with Mar about 3.9¢ over; that wide carry into Dec delivery says the market expects certificated cotton to show up, which is not a comfortable backdrop for Dec longs.
events: Trade deals seen opening room for more US cotton and rice exports (Brownfield)
Texas growers squeezed by high fuel costs and poor yields (RFD-TV, Farm Progress)
USDA trimmed its cotton crop estimate earlier this week (Brownfield)

sugar.fundamental: Brazil drives it: the post-election slide in the real raises mills' returns on exports in local currency and encourages sugar-heavy mixes, while raw sugar still pays above ethanol parity. Friday's bounce back over 18.4¢ is short covering on firmer crude, not a change in the Brazilian supply picture.
events: Raw sugar dropped with the Brazilian real on Thursday (Barchart)
Mar holds around 18.39, near the 18.35–18.38 resistance, midday Friday (desk quote)
Crude strength earlier in the week sparked short covering (Barchart)

coffee.fundamental: ICE certified arabica keeps drawing (about 229k bags, down ~6% in a month), which supports Dec into delivery; against that, Brazil's exports have jumped and a weaker real speeds farmer selling, so more deliverable coffee is on the way. Net: near-term tightness at the exchange versus a looser Brazil flow.
events: Low ICE inventories lifted arabica to ~280 Thursday; Dec probed 285.75 Friday before slipping back (Barchart, TradingView)
Brazil coffee exports up sharply year on year (ADMIS, Barchart)
Brazilian real weakness weighing on prices (Barchart)

cocoa.fundamental: Weather is back as a supply risk: excessive rain in Ivory Coast is slowing harvest and port arrivals, and the national weather agency warned El Niño could cut output by up to a quarter. Rising ICE stocks and industry estimates of a 2025/26 surplus keep the balance comfortable for now, so the risk is in next season's mid-crop.
events: Heavy Ivory Coast rains disrupt cocoa flows and lift prices (Barchart)
Ivory Coast weather agency warns El Niño could cut production ~25% (Reuters, ADMIS)
Dec cocoa holds gains near 5,130 midday Friday (desk quote)
